title: Leitvia skill scenario
description: One task a human gives an agent, the ability calls that solve it without a language model and the end state they must leave. Run by packages/leitvia-skills/tests/run-scenarios.mjs against a fresh Playground. Placeholders {{capture.<name>}} in inputs take values captured by earlier steps.

skill.description: Folder name of the skill under skills/, or smoke for checks of the gateway itself; equals the folder of the scenario. Scenarios under workflows/ name the workflow instead, for example new-site.

briefing.description: The task in plain English, as a human would give it to the agent.

mode.description: direct: the autonomy of the site applies. package: every write of the task goes into one change package.

tags.description: Labels to count scenarios apart, for example commerce for scenarios that need WooCommerce.

answers.description: Answers of the human at the checkpoints of the skill, keyed by checkpoint. Used by agent runs, ignored by the runner.

attachments.description: Files the person hands over with the briefing, as paths under tests/fixtures/. Agent runs copy them into the working folder of the agent; the runner ignores them.

setup.description: Extra blueprint steps after dev/playground/blueprint.json, for example fixture content or WooCommerce.

steps.description: Ability calls in order, made as the user agent over REST.

user.description: admin: the person at a checkpoint, for example applying a change package. Needs a setup step that writes the application password of user 1 to /leitvia-run/admin-password.txt.

capture.description: Name to dot path in the response, for example "hash" or "data.current_hash" of a rejection.

expectError.description: Rejection code the call must end in.

expect.description: End state: ability calls with expected fields, or public URLs with status, number of h1 and strings the page contains. Also checked against the result of an agent run (--expect-only).

h1.description: Number of h1 elements on the page.

contains.description: Strings the HTML of the page must contain, for example every sentence of a migrated post.

match.description: Dot path in the response to the expected value. A value is compared deeply; an object with one operator compares otherwise: $gte, $lte, $exists, $match (regular expression). The path items.length is the length of an array.
